domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's request for leave. Central entity of the leave management module. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through approval/rejection to cancellation, including who acted and when.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — Employee is composing the request; not yet visible to managers. Only the owning employee can see or modify it.
SUBMITTED — Request has been submitted and is pending manager review. Visible to the employee and their manager chain.
APPROVED — Manager has approved the request. Balance has been deducted. The leave is confirmed.
REJECTED — Manager has rejected the request with a reason. No balance impact. Employee may revise and resubmit.
CANCELLED — A previously SUBMITTED or APPROVED request has been cancelled. If previously APPROVED, balance is restored.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequestStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of lifecycle states for a LeaveRequest. Drives all state-transition validation and determines which actions are available at each stage.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT → SUBMITTED (transition: submit) — Employee finalises and sends the request for manager review.
DRAFT → CANCELLED (transition: discard) — Employee discards a draft they no longer need.
SUBMITTED → APPROVED (transition: approve) — Manager approves the request. Balance is deducted.
SUBMITTED → REJECTED (transition: reject) — Manager rejects the request with a mandatory reason.
SUBMITTED → CANCELLED (transition: withdraw) — Employee withdraws a submitted request before a decision.
APPROVED → CANCELLED (transition: cancelApproved) — Employee or manager cancels an already-approved leave. Balance is restored.
REJECTED → DRAFT (transition: revise) — Employee reopens a rejected request to edit and resubmit.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Categorises leave requests (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity). Each type carries flags that influence validation rules — e.g. whether documentation is required or whether the leave is paid.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Leave type is available for employees to request.
INACTIVE — Leave type has been soft-disabled; no new requests can use it, but historical records remain.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type. Each policy specifies entitlement, accrual behaviour, notice requirements, and approval rules. Referenced by Balance to determine remaining entitlement and by LeaveRequest validation to enforce constraints.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Policy is in effect; leave requests are validated against it and balances are computed from it.
INACTIVE — Policy has been retired; no new requests or balances reference it, but historical data is preserved.

domain_entities.name: Balance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave type within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave requests are approved or cancelled. One Balance row per employee per leave type per fiscal year.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Balance is in effect for the current fiscal year; leave requests draw from it.
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays has reached zero; no further requests can be approved unless the policy allows negative balance.
CLOSED — Fiscal year has ended; balance is archived and immutable. A new ACTIVE balance is created for the next fiscal year.

domain_entities.name: BalanceStatus
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of lifecycle states for a Balance record. Controls whether the balance can be drawn upon for new leave requests.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE
EXHAUSTED
CLOSED

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee in the organisation. Acts as the actor who requests leave and the manager who approves/rejects. Employment status gates whether the employee can submit leave requests.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — Employee is currently employed and can submit leave requests.
INACTIVE — Employee is on extended leave or suspension; cannot submit new leave requests but existing requests remain valid.
TERMINATED — Employee has left the organisation; all access revoked, no new requests allowed, historical data preserved.

business_rules: BR-001 — LeaveRequest submission: An employee may only submit a LeaveRequest if their employmentStatus is ACTIVE. The startDate must be on or after today. The endDate must be on or after startDate. The leaveTypeId must reference an ACTIVE LeaveType whose associated LeavePolicy is ACTIVE.

BR-003 — Balance deduction on approval: When a LeaveRequest transitions from SUBMITTED to APPROVED, the corresponding Balance.usedDays is incremented by the number of leave days, and Balance.remainingDays is decremented accordingly. If remainingDays reaches zero, the Balance transitions to EXHAUSTED. This must happen atomically within the same transaction.

BR-002 — LeaveRequest overlap detection: A new SUBMITTED LeaveRequest must not overlap in date range with any existing APPROVED or SUBMITTED LeaveRequest for the same employee. Overlap is defined as: existing.startDate <= new.endDate AND existing.endDate >= new.startDate.

BR-004 — Balance restoration on cancellation: When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the previously deducted days are restored: Balance.usedDays is decremented and Balance.remainingDays is incremented by the same amount. If the Balance was EXHAUSTED, it transitions back to ACTIVE. This must happen atomically within the same transaction.

BR-005 — Sufficient balance check: Before a LeaveRequest can be approved, the employee must have sufficient remainingDays in their Balance for the requested leaveTypeId and fiscalYear. If remainingDays < requestedDays and the LeavePolicy.allowNegativeBalance is false, the approval must be rejected. If allowNegativeBalance is true, the balance may go negative.

BR-007 — Maximum consecutive days: If LeavePolicy.maximumConsecutiveDays is set, the LeaveRequest duration (endDate - startDate + 1) must not exceed that value. This prevents abuse of leave types intended for short absences (e.g. emergency leave).

BR-008 — Manager approval authority: Only the employee's designated manager (Employee.managerId) or a user with the HR_ADMIN role may approve or reject a LeaveRequest. Self-approval is prohibited — the approver's employeeId must differ from the LeaveRequest.employeeId.

BR-009 — Rejection requires reason: When a LeaveRequest is rejected, rejectionReason is mandatory. The rejection must be recorded with rejectedBy (the manager's employeeId) and rejectedAt (timestamp).
